chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Arriving in Oklahoma City: sitting in with the band and its gentlemen
summary: At first she was only John's wife, driving and called in to play 'Froggy Bottom' when the band was stuck. She remembers the musicians as young, well-dressed gentlemen.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So we got into Oklahoma City. After I arrived, the boys were dissatisfied about T. Holder and they called a meeting -
Did you join the band to play?

No, I was there as John's wife but he was very shrewd about it. He had his way of working me in. The pianist was very, very great but not as exciting. He was more of a - how shall I say it? - legit pianist, very beautiful chords and very wonderful pianist. So what I did was to go out on trips with them and when they were stuck - I'd sit in the instrumental truck, I'd drive a car or the instrumental truck or something - and if they got stuck and weren't going over big they'd call me in to do "Froggy Bottom" or something.
Were you doing "Froggy Bottom" by then?

Well, there were other tunes similar to that, but "Froggy Bottom" later, about a year later it was written. Before we even recorded it, you know. So we did this for quite a while and I traveled with the band and I'd sit in and play with him. After we played Oklahoma City, played one-nighters and all down through the Indian Territory. This was very exciting for me. We decided to leave. One thing I wanted to tell you - there was the most handsome - the boys were the most handsome guys and the most wonderful gentlemen that I've ever met. I don't think any one of them was over 25 or 26 years old but they were so well trained. Most of them were college graduates or something and they dressed very fine and they were so respectful of people. I've never been around a group like that, of musicians.
